entries.title: The changelog, public
entries.summary: This page: how the site got the way it is, the choices with their alternatives, and the comps beside the shipped thing. A quiet link in the footer.

entries.title: A page for the people who were in the room
entries.summary: After the Orlando workshop: Amy’s note, the photos from the class, and a Back in the studio section. Unlisted: no index, no nav, no sitemap. The site chrome stays.

entries.title: The same printed QR, retargeted
entries.summary: The event page keeps one fixed address. Per stop, the facts change, the order source changes, and the show discount is reactivated for the window.

entries.title: Every FAQ answer has its own address
entries.summary: An anchor per question, opening on arrival, so a reply can point at one answer.

entries.title: Email capture waits behind a switch
entries.summary: Capture blocks in the footer and at the tail of posts render nothing until the switch flips after Amy’s aesthetic pass.
entries.note: Advance to the endpoint; pause at the aesthetic call.

entries.title: A landing for the YouTube description
entries.summary: A seen-it-on-YouTube hero, a video embed once one is picked, a channel-scoped first-month offer, email capture. Unlisted.

entries.title: The expired price comes off the page
entries.summary: The re-collection page headlined an offer three weeks past its deadline. It shows the regular price honestly now.

entries.title: The first envelope, promised by date
entries.summary: The line under the plan cards computes which month’s envelope your order funds, from today’s date. The wording went to Amy as a veto line before it merged.

entries.title: International shipping, said before you pay
entries.summary: One line in the cart drawer: international orders ship at live USPS rates by weight, shown at checkout. No rate hardcoded.

entries.title: Start here: twenty posts, chosen from the data
entries.summary: Pageviews over 120 days plus a spread across DIY, journaling, encouragement, and lettering. Near-duplicate guest layouts and personal recaps skipped.

figures.alt: The Journal index with the Start here picks on top
figures.caption: The Journal, Start here on top.

entries.title: Dropdowns that open on a tap
entries.summary: iPad portrait is the desktop breakpoint, and touch has no hover. First tap opens the menu, second follows the link; mouse behavior unchanged.

entries.title: The camera comes on when the page loads
entries.summary: The August 4 tap gate made visitors hit the button before the camera woke. Used live, the original behavior came back, with a guard for a missing stream.

options.title: Tap to start the camera
options.blurb: Permission is per origin and sticky; one reflexive Block would kill the camera for the whole site.

options.title: Prompt on load, guard the missing stream
options.blurb: The flag stays as the one-word switch.

entries.title: Real subscribers replace the placeholder quotes
entries.summary: Four subscribers in their own words, first name and last initial, from one shared array for every page that shows them.

entries.title: The photobooth moves onto the site
entries.summary: Its own repo, project, and subdomain retire; the booth becomes a route under Fun Stuff, and the old subdomain redirects here for good.
entries.note: New experiments are built as routes under the Fun Stuff nav, not as new subdomains.

figures.caption: The booth as a route on the site.

options.title: Its own subdomain, its own repo
options.blurb: Reachable only as an external nav link; no measurement at all.

options.title: A route on the site
options.blurb: Look and behavior preserved; the wordmark hides on phones, where the nav already carries it.

entries.title: A collaboration leads the faves page
entries.summary: A three-item collection opens Shop My Faves. Single-list refreshes can no longer clobber edits on the others.

entries.title: One cutoff: the 15th
entries.summary: The first-envelope FAQ lands on both Happy Mail pages, and the cancel answer that said “before the 5th” now agrees with it.

entries.title: help@ for orders, hello@ for everything else
entries.summary: The contact page splits by inbox, and the subject-line routing goes.

figures.alt: The contact page with two inboxes
figures.caption: Two doors, said plainly.

entries.title: In Person, and three things in the nav
entries.summary: Events redesigned and renamed In Person: upcoming first, city-led cards, recap video slots. The header becomes Fun Stuff, Shop, About Amy.
entries.note: Three top-level items: Fun Stuff (a dropdown, room to grow), Shop, About Amy.

entries.title: A friendlier 404
entries.summary: A dead link lands on a page that helps: three current products, the Journal, a search, the way home.

entries.title: Shop My Faves nests under Shop; My Books joins
entries.summary: The affiliate page becomes a child of Shop, and Amy’s own titles get a section.

entries.title: The Journal comes back
entries.summary: The blog is reinstated with curation and hygiene: legacy paths redirect, thin posts fold, the archive gets a search.

entries.title: Shop My Faves
entries.summary: An affiliate page with its own data model behind it: real lists, deep links, images populated from the source.

entries.title: Printables get their own tab
entries.summary: A category tab in the shop, excluded from the default grid. A gated preview for drafts follows.

figures.alt: The shop with the Printables tab selected
figures.caption: The Printables tab.

entries.title: Tokyo Takeover: the gallery and the waitlist
entries.summary: Real photos from Tokyo and Amy’s copy; the waitlist asks for one name field to match the list it feeds.

entries.title: Events collapse to one landing page
entries.summary: The separate pages fold into a single events surface with a regrounded voice and verified details.

entries.title: amytangerine.com goes live
entries.summary: DNS flips from Squarespace on the target Friday and the gate comes off. Eight weeks from scaffold to launch.

entries.title: Happy Mail: four tiles, fan mail, the truth about six months
entries.summary: The hero becomes four real photos of what arrives. “From the mailbox” becomes “Fan mail.” The six-month copy says what it is: a renewing commitment.

entries.title: The cosmetic pass, with Amy at the desk
entries.summary: The hero becomes the Shine Bright mural shot; the tagline goes full white and bigger. Category tiles get real product shots; the spotlight gets Paper Play 3.

figures.alt: Amy in front of the Shine Bright mural
figures.caption: The mural shot, Amy’s pick.

entries.title: Five Instagram posts, in Amy’s order
entries.summary: Six product-photo placeholders give way to five posts she chose, in her order, linking out to her feed.

entries.title: Every month, a letter from me
entries.summary: Amy picks Option A for Happy Mail: a product-grid hero of what’s in the envelope, plan cards in the same viewport, every button straight to cart. Hand-lettering leaves the marketing.

figures.alt: The April wireframe of the Happy Mail landing page
figures.caption: The April wireframe.

figures.alt: The Happy Mail page as shipped
figures.caption: Option A, shipped.

options.title: The April landing: split hero, the big stamp graphic, pricing below
options.blurb: Pricing cards, What’s Inside, How It Works, a gallery, the FAQ. Photos were placeholders.

options.title: Option A: the product-grid hero
options.blurb: Die cuts, sticker sheet, envelope, note: the box contents above the fold, plans right under.

entries.title: Contact stays out of the nav
entries.summary: The Contact link added to the mobile drawer the night before comes back out. Happy Mail at the top of the drawer stays.
entries.note: Don’t incent contact: keep the nav focused on shop, subscribe, brand story.

entries.title: The favicon is the tangerine slice
entries.summary: Amy’s existing favicon, pulled from the old site and mirrored byte for byte, so the brand survives the cutover in the tab.

entries.title: Seven fixes from friends and family
entries.summary: The checkout button resets after eight seconds instead of sticking. Empty categories drop and the grid goes to three. “Image coming soon” replaces the gray box.

entries.title: An About page, and thirty-two logos
entries.summary: Bio, values, and a collaborations wall of thirty-two brand logos in Amy’s own order, where a text list of six had stood.

figures.alt: The collaborations logo wall on the About page
figures.caption: The collaborations wall.

entries.title: The logo is the wordmark
entries.summary: The text wordmark in the nav gives way to Amy’s own logo image, the slice and the tagline.

entries.title: D3: editorial, with color
entries.summary: Seven homepages on staging, each built to test one question. Amy picked D3 on April 14: the cinematic hero with teal and orange section grounds.

figures.alt: The teal category grid on the homepage
figures.caption: D3 shipped: the teal category grid.

options.title: v2 Current
options.blurb: The control: the existing layout with the real colors and font.

options.title: Amy’s World
options.blurb: A portal to everything she does: books, workshops, podcast; a personal headline.

options.title: Craft Feel
options.blurb: Hand-drawn accents, softer cards, a warm overlay. Personality over grid.

options.title: Editorial
options.blurb: Cinematic hero, tight density, ghost buttons.

options.title: Editorial + Playful
options.blurb: D with squiggly underlines and doodles.

options.title: Editorial + Promo
options.blurb: D with a Happy Mail conversion hero.

options.title: Editorial + Color
options.blurb: D with teal and orange section backgrounds.

entries.title: Eight nav items become three, and Happy Mail gets a button
entries.summary: The old nav had eight items and no Happy Mail at all. The new one: Shop, Photobooth, About, and a Happy Mail button that never leaves the header.

entries.title: Shop, cart, and product pages
entries.summary: A catalog from Shopify, the shop grid, product pages, and a cart drawer with a count badge. Prices live from the store, never typed in.

entries.title: The Happy Mail landing page
entries.summary: A page instead of a product listing: pricing cards, What’s Inside, How It Works, past months, testimonials, the FAQ. Every subscribe button measured.

entries.title: The real brand, not the wireframe’s guess
entries.summary: One orange, not two; a brighter teal; pure white and true black; Epilogue. Pulled from the live site instead of estimated.

options.title: The wireframe palette
options.blurb: Golden and coral oranges, a sage teal, cream paper, Nunito Sans.

options.title: The live site’s own tokens
options.blurb: #FD891C, #00ADB3, white, black, Epilogue. Not a creative choice: her brand.

entries.title: A prototype instead of a Figma file
entries.summary: Wireframes as HTML pages, then a Next.js scaffold the same day. Amy reviews a working site, not a mockup.
